title: 2026 Climate Tech Companies to Watch
gist: MIT Technology Review's fourth annual 2026 Climate Tech Companies to Watch list names 10 firms: Energy Dome, WaveSave, Envision Energy, Brimstone, Fervo Energy, WeLion New Energy, BasiGo, Form Energy, X-energy and Moment Energy, spanning storage, flood barriers, wind, cement, geothermal, EVs and nuclear.

insights.claim: Three of the ten 2026 picks are energy storage companies (Energy Dome in Milan, WeLion New Energy in Beijing, Form Energy in Somerville), plus Moment Energy in battery repurposing, making storage the most represented category.
insights.speaker: Amy Nordrum
insights.so_what: Editorial consensus sees storage as the pivotal climate-tech segment this year.

insights.claim: Only four of the ten companies are US-based (Brimstone, Fervo Energy, Form Energy, X-energy), with the rest in Italy, the Netherlands, China (two), Kenya and Canada.
insights.speaker: Amy Nordrum
insights.so_what: Geographic diversification of the climate-tech frontier away from the US.

insights.claim: The list spans clean firm power (Fervo geothermal, X-energy nuclear fission), industrial decarbonization (Brimstone heavy industry/cement), adaptation (WaveSave flood barriers), and African EV adoption (BasiGo, Nairobi).
insights.speaker: Amy Nordrum
insights.so_what: Breadth signals editors see investable progress across both mitigation and adaptation.
insights.quote: From energy storage powered by carbon dioxide to cleaner ways to make cement and refine critical minerals

insights.claim: Fervo Energy is on the list for a third year, while Envision Energy, BasiGo and Form Energy are marked as second-year entrants.
insights.speaker: Amy Nordrum
insights.so_what: Repeat selection suggests sustained execution, especially for Fervo's enhanced geothermal.

insights.claim: The list includes both incumbents and startups: founding years range from Envision Energy (2007) and X-energy (2009) to BasiGo (2021).
insights.speaker: Amy Nordrum
insights.so_what: Climate-tech champions now include mature scaled players, not just venture-stage startups.
insights.quote: Whether early-stage startup or multinational corporation
